meeting.title: Vector × Ashby — embedded analytics kickoff
meeting.summary: Kickoff for the Ashby embedded analytics rollout. They run dbt Core on Snowflake, repo on GitHub, and are moving reporting off Mode. The distinguishing requirement is that Ashby wants to embed Vector dashboards inside their own product for their customers, not just use them internally — so row-level permissions are a first-class concern rather than an afterthought. Nate wants the executive KPI dashboard internally first to prove parity, then embedding. fct_pipeline is the anchor fact table. Access was agreed with no obstacles and Ritu committed to having everything provisioned within the week.
action_items: Ritu to provision a read-only Snowflake service account scoped to the ANALYTICS schema
Ritu to add Vector Cloud static IPs to the Snowflake network policy
Ritu to grant Vector read access to the dbt project repo on GitHub
Caroline to send the implementation plan and weekly sync invite
Nate to confirm which customer-facing metrics are in scope for embedding
key_decisions: Internal parity first, customer-facing embedding second — embedding does not start until parity is signed off
fct_pipeline is the first fact table to get a metrics block
Okta is the SSO provider; row-level permissions are in scope from day one, not deferred
meeting.notes: Different shape to our usual onboarding — the end users are Ashby's customers, not Ashby's staff, so permissions and multi-tenancy are the real project. Nate is pragmatic and clear about sequencing. Ritu is fast and unblocked. Low-risk account on current evidence.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Thanks for the time. I want to spend most of this on the embedding requirement, because it makes your project meaningfully different from a standard rollout.

transcript.speaker: Nate Coleman
transcript.text: Agreed, and I'm glad you led with that. The internal use case is real but it's not the reason we bought. Our customers want analytics inside Ashby, and right now we hand-build every one of those views.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: So the end user is a recruiter at one of your customers, looking at their own hiring pipeline, inside your product.

transcript.speaker: Nate Coleman
transcript.text: Exactly. And they must never, under any circumstances, see another customer's data.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: Then row-level permissions aren't a phase-three nicety, they're load-bearing from the first dashboard. That changes how I'd sequence this.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: It does. Nate, how do you want to order it? My instinct is prove parity internally before you put anything in front of a paying customer.

transcript.speaker: Nate Coleman
transcript.text: That's my instinct too. If our own exec dashboard doesn't match Mode, I'm certainly not shipping it to customers. Internal parity first. Embedding second.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: Ritu, what's underneath? Warehouse, repo, models?

transcript.speaker: Ritu Sharma
transcript.text: Snowflake, dbt Core, GitHub. Around eighty models. fct_pipeline is the one you want — it's every candidate stage transition and it's what every customer question ultimately reduces to.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: Then that's where the first metrics block goes. What do you need from us to get me access?

transcript.speaker: Ritu Sharma
transcript.text: Nothing, I can just do it. Read-only service account on ANALYTICS, your IPs on the network policy, repo read access. I'll have it done this week.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: That is a refreshingly short answer.

transcript.speaker: Ritu Sharma
transcript.text: We're a small team. There's nobody to ask.

transcript.speaker: Nate Coleman
transcript.text: One thing I do need to go away and figure out — exactly which metrics we're comfortable exposing to customers. Some of what's in fct_pipeline is benchmarking data across our whole book, and that's commercially sensitive.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: That's an important call and it's yours to make, not ours. Can you come back with a scoped list of customer-facing metrics before we start the embedding phase?

transcript.speaker: Nate Coleman
transcript.text: Yes. I'll have it well before you need it.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Perfect. I'll send the plan and a weekly sync. Ritu, ping us the moment access lands and Theo will start the same day.
